en.text: JoeRunner and T.T. see the new kid in class.

fr.text: JoeRunner et T.T. voient la petite nouvelle en classe.

en.text: JoeRunner and T.T. walk through a door. A desk with a desktop computer and a sheet of paper folded into a triangle reading “Mr. Mahan.” T.T. looks confused and a bit annoyed. JoeRunner looks at him amusedly.

en.html: But, like . . . how come no one told me?

en.text: JoeRunner and T.T. go to their seats next to each other. T.T. points backward.
Oh, hey, I think the new kid is back there.
The new kid is writing a letter at her desk, just finishing her signature. She has medium‑length red (orange) hair. She wears a dark turquoise shirt.

en.html:
Dear Mr. Mahan, Thank you very much for having me for the last two weeks of school. I look forward to it. That is all I have to say.

—⁠Ma
(off‑panel) Oh, darn, I forgot to get her name from Harry.

en.text: JoeRunner starts getting out of his seat.
Well then, let’s go ask her!
JoeRunner and T.T. look back, a little disappointed.
Oh, well, I guess she’ll introduce herself first.
Lucky number 11! People . . . people probably say that.

I was initially meaning to upload the full‐size versions to Patreon, but I’ll probably just save that for the .clip work files. I don’t know when I’ll get the images out, but I will.

Of course, you can safely expect Patreon to be a pretty long ways away at this rate. If I can be real for a sec, one of the main reasons I started this comic was to feel like I was doing something with my life, and now it’s ended up as a huge source of anxiety for me because progress is so slow. I’m so excited to continue this, especially since I have a lot of other ideas to work on aside from JoeRunner and co.⁠—both apart from and on top of it. I’m so sorry that I’m not getting that out sooner.

en.text: Um . . . on an unrelated note, color! I haven’t been using color so far because I had the notion that it would take too long, but I wanted that panel to be better‐drawn anyway, so I went ahead and did it. And now I’m thinking maybe I should do that more often.

en.html: On a dumb, overthinking‐related note (feel free to skip this), I’m trying to decide if I want to stick with CC BY‑SA 4.0, or if I want to move it to CC BY. At the start it was BY‑NC‑SA. Both times the SA was because I wanted to keep derivatives of actual, general utility free, like books and translations. I know that Pepper&Carrot is thriving in those regards under CC BY, but that may or may not be different, considering that Pepper&Carrot isn’t one of the most egregious abominations known to man.

And about those multiple image size problems, I want to make a Git repository to hold all of those (and the other stuff, of course) in order to have a sort of structured, static API, while also just having the files available in a human‐browsable and easily downloadable manner. I already tried that with files.gabl.ink [link removed], but I ended up not liking how it turned out.
